conventions.commits: Conventional commits with scope and issue number suffix, e.g. 'feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)'. Every commit carries a 'Signed-off-by:' DCO trailer; recent commits show a GPG signature (git log %G? returns E in the clone, meaning signed but unverifiable here).
conventions.testing: Unit tests in a #[cfg(test)] mod tests block inside each languages/<lang>.rs (queries_compile, set_language_smoke, element_query_matches_*, extract_inheritance_*); table tests in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs; table-driven integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs (ImportTestCase); MCP-level tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw and tempfile.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity; workspace lints deny undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test code exempt via cfg_attr); cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; .github/scripts/check-package-age.sh; REUSE compliance (SPDX header in every new file).
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option<String> or Vec<String>; node text is read through the bounds-checked get_node_text helper in languages/mod.rs or an end_byte <= source.len() guard; missing nodes yield None or an empty Vec; no unwrap/expect in non-test code; query compile errors surface as ParserError.

patterns: Each language module exports ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and DEFUSE_QUERY as &'static str constants with a doc comment, plus optional handler functions (extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance).

Element captures use fixed names: @function wraps the whole declaration; @func_name or @method_name, and @class_name or @type_name, carry the identifier; @class wraps type declarations (parser_elements.rs L262-L330). Java uses @class for interface and enum as well as class.

DEFUSE_QUERY capture names carry the kind as a prefix: write.* is a definition, read.* is a use, writeread.* is an update. Reads at the same byte offset as a write are dropped (parser_elements.rs L878-L894).

extract_inheritance returns prefixed strings: Java uses 'extends X' and 'implements X'; Swift uses 'extends X' and 'conforms X'. The handler is invoked on the class-like node itself (parser_elements.rs L398-L404).
Registry is a match on the language name in get_language_info (full LanguageInfo) and in get_ts_language (Language only); the extension lookup is a const EXTENSION_MAP slice in lang.rs.
Each grammar crate is pinned once in the root [workspace.dependencies] and referenced as { workspace = true } in crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml.

Languages whose tree-sitter grammar has no node for a capability set the handler to None (e.g. css and yaml have no extract_inheritance, fortran and markdown have no defuse_query); this is a valid pattern for partial support.
Every new source file starts with two SPDX lines (FileCopyrightText and License-Identifier) and a //! or /// module doc comment.

constraints: Issue #1864 states external pull requests are not accepted; the maintainers implement it in-house. This research is for internal planning only.

The issue's acceptance criteria require: EXTENSION_MAP entry, supported_languages() entry, get_language_info and get_ts_language arms, php.rs with the five queries and extract_inheritance, unit tests, one integration test, README update, and cargo deny passing without SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK.

supported_languages() in lang.rs (L81-L99) must contain 'php': parser.rs L183-L195 builds QUERY_CACHE only from that list, so PHP would have no compiled-query slot otherwise. css is absent from that list, so it is not a complete template here.
Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP (the php grammar with HTML text outside <?php tags), not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, because acceptance requires a mixed HTML/PHP file to parse with zero ERROR nodes.
extract_inheritance must not use child_by_field_name('superclass') or ('interfaces'): tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 has no such fields; base_clause and class_interface_clause are unfielded children.

The grammar's class rules use 'name' fields, and method and function declarations use 'name' fields; PHP variables are variable_name nodes containing a name child, so DEFUSE captures must target the inner name node to match symbol text without the leading dollar sign.
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used in non-test code; new code must use the bounds-checked helpers or Option combinators.
New Cargo.lock packages must be at least 7 days old (check-package-age.sh); tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 is the latest GitHub release tag and its crates.io publish date was not verified.

Scope exclusions from the issue: no extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver or find_receiver_type; no trait use resolution, property or constant extraction, attributes, or namespace alias handling; no .phtml, .inc, .module or .php5 extensions; no tool-handler or schema changes.
test_coverage: Every existing language module has inline unit tests (swift.rs: queries_compile, set_language_smoke, element_query_matches_class_and_function, extract_inheritance_superclass_and_protocols, extract_inheritance_no_inheritance; css.rs: rule-set element, import and empty-file tests; java.rs: extract_function_name and similar). languages/mod.rs tests get_language_info_known, get_language_info_unknown, get_ts_language_known and a table test covering tsx, fortran, markdown, css and yaml; there is no php or java entry there. lang.rs tests language_for_extension happy and edge paths and the schema pattern covering all extensions, which means adding 'php' to EXTENSION_MAP automatically extends that test. parser.rs has a lazy-compile test using supported_languages().len(). integration_tests.rs has table-driven import tests for Go and Java (L1536-L1660). I did not run cargo test: this run is read-only and the research did not require a build.

The grammar's README-level example from bindings/rust/lib.rs: "let language = tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP;" then "parser.set_language(&language.into())". php/grammar.js is a stub: its literal content is "const defineGrammar = require('../common/define-grammar.js');" followed by "module.exports = defineGrammar('php');", so the real rules are in common/define-grammar.js.

library_findings.relevant_api: pub fn Query::new(language: &Language, source: &str) -> Result<Self, QueryError> (confirmed via Context7 /websites/rs_tree-sitter); Parser::set_language, QueryCursor::matches, StreamingIterator for matches.next(), Node::child_by_field_name, Node::named_child, Node::child, Node::kind, Node::start_byte and end_byte.
library_findings.notes: Queries are compiled against a Language; a bad field name or node kind makes Query::new return Err, which is the basis for the queries_compile test. Existing modules use the same API via tree_sitter::{Parser, StreamingIterator}.

approaches.name: A: Full Java-style handler with DEFUSE_QUERY and child-walk inheritance (recommended)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type name), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (parameter, static, global, assignment, compound assignment, update, and bare name reads), and extract_inheritance that iterates unfielded base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Wire 'php' into lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages, language_for_extension test), languages/mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info with defuse_query Some, get_ts_language, doc list), root and core Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, README, and add integration tests plus a mixed-HTML test.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in #1864, including extends/implements output and HTML-template behaviour.
DEFUSE_QUERY gives find-definition and use-site results for PHP, matching Java, Kotlin, Swift, C#, C++, Python, JavaScript and TypeScript.
Follows the Swift and Java registry shape exactly, so review is mechanical.
Inheritance handler is grammar-accurate: it reads node kinds, not nonexistent fields.
cons: DEFUSE_QUERY relies on name-text matching, so $this->x and bare function names can produce false read sites for a local variable of the same name.
Several query patterns cannot be validated without compiling against the grammar; the unit tests are the only check.
New Cargo.lock entry must pass the 7-day package-age rule.

approaches.name: B: Minimal handler (element, call, import only)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY, set REFERENCE_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance to None (as fortran, css and yaml do), and wire the registry the same way as Approach A.
pros: Smallest diff; fewest query patterns to verify.
Lower risk of false read sites since no defuse query is present.
cons: Fails the issue's acceptance criteria for extends/implements output and for a symbol's definition and use sites.
Leaves PHP unlike every other OO language in the registry (Java, Kotlin, Swift, C#, C++ all supply inheritance).
The second pass would still need the same DEFUSE and inheritance work.

approaches.name: C: Seed queries from the grammar's own queries/tags.scm
approaches.description: Take ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY from the upstream queries/tags.scm (exposed as tree_sitter_php::TAGS_QUERY) instead of hand-writing them, then add the DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance by hand. Not inspected in this run: the file's content and capture names were not fetched, so this approach is unverified.
pros: Uses node kinds the grammar maintainers already exercise.
cons: Upstream tags.scm capture names (name, definition.function, reference.call) do not match aptu-coder capture names (function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name), so they still need renaming.
Upstream tags.scm may include patterns that produce duplicate elements in parser_elements.rs.
Adds a dependency on a non-stable query file.

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets the issue's acceptance criteria (extends/implements output, HTML-template zero-ERROR parse, define-use results), and it mirrors the Java and Swift integrations. DEFUSE_QUERY is required because parser_elements.rs L850-L852 returns an empty vector when compiled.defuse is None, so a PHP without DEFUSE_QUERY would return no definition or use sites for any symbol, unlike the other OO languages. Use LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) so text outside <?php tags parses without ERROR nodes. Write extract_inheritance as a child walk, not as a copy of Java's field-based code.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source inspected: tree-sitter-php tag v0.25.2. (1) common/define-grammar.js (php/grammar.js is a stub that calls defineGrammar('php') from this file). class_declaration rule, L365-L375: seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list)). base_clause, L334-L337: seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). class_interface_clause, L381-L384: seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)). _name, L296-L302: choice(alias(keyword('static', false), $.name), alias(choice(...CAST_TYPE_CLASS_NAMES...), $.name), reserved('classes', $.name), $.qualified_name, $.relative_name). (2) php/src/node-types.json, class_declaration entry: fields are exactly attributes, body and name; there is no superclass, interfaces, base_clauses or parent_class field. Its children types include base_clause and class_interface_clause, both unfielded. base_clause children types: name, qualified_name, relative_name. class_interface_clause children types: name, qualified_name, relative_name. (3) Context7 (tree-sitter-php grammar docs) quotes the same rules and a corpus example: 'class Exception_foo implements ThrowableInterface' parses as class_declaration with name: (name), (class_interface_clause (name)), body: (declaration_list ...). Field-by-field walk for class_declaration node N: (a) N.child_by_field_name('name') gives the class identifier (name field, kind name). (b) Iterate N's children by index (no field name). For each child C with C.kind() == 'base_clause', iterate C's named children (the extends keyword is anonymous, so it is skipped) and emit 'extends ' + text for each child of kind name, qualified_name or relative_name. (c) For each child C with C.kind() == 'class_interface_clause', iterate its named children and emit 'implements ' + text for each child of kind name, qualified_name or relative_name. Expected output for 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}' is ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; for 'class Plain {}' it is []. The same child walk handles interface_declaration (base_clause only, L326-L332), enum_declaration (class_interface_clause only, L339-L345) and trait_declaration (no clause). Java's child_by_field_name('superclass') and ('interfaces') calls would return None for every PHP node.
